<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

**Multiplication and Division**

Here is the correct answer to a multiplication problem:

$6 \times 5678 \times 10 = 340680$

Use this information to help you work out the answer to this division problem:

$340680 \div 5678$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">**Multiplication and Division**
<emptyline>
Here is the correct answer to a multiplication problem:
<emptyline>
$6 \times 5678 \times 10 = 340680$
<emptyline>
Use this information to help you work out the answer to this division problem:
<emptyline>
$340680 \div 5678$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

\begin{aligned}
&= 340680 \div 5678 \\\\
&= \dfrac{340680}{5678} \\\\
&= \dfrac{ 6 \times 5678 \times 10}{5678} \\\\
&= \dfrac{\cancel{5678} \times 6 \times 10}{\cancel{5678}} \\\\
&= 6 \times 10 \\\\
&= 60
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

**Working**

Let the missing number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
7000 \div 100                                &= 700 \div a \\\\
\dfrac{7000}{100}                            &= \dfrac{700}{a} \\\\
a \times \dfrac{7000}{100}                   &= 700 \\\\
a                                            &= \dfrac{700 \times 100}{7000} \\\\
a                                            &= \dfrac{7000 \times 10}{7000} \\\\
a                                            &= \dfrac{\cancel{7000} \times 10}{\cancel{7000}} \\\\
70                                           &= 10
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$\approx$ means approximately equal to. Given that $1\ \text{kilogram (kg)} \approx 2·2\ \text{pounds (lb)}$, convert $154\ \text{lb}$ to $\text{kg}$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$\approx$ means approximately equal to. Given that $1\ \text{kilogram (kg)} \approx 2·2\ \text{pounds (lb)}$, convert $154\ \text{lb}$ to $\text{kg}$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 154 \ \text{lb} \\\\
&= 154 \times \dfrac{1}{2.2} \ \text{kg} \\\\
&= \dfrac{154}{2.2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{154 \times 10}{2.2 \times 10} \\\\
&= \dfrac{154 \times 10}{22} \\\\
&= \dfrac{7 \times 22 \times 10}{22} \\\\
&= \dfrac{7 \times \cancel{22} \times 10}{\cancel{22}} \\\\
&= 7 \times 10  \\\\
&= 70 \ \text{kg}
\end{aligned} 
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$70 \ \text{kg}$

</div>
</div>

A palindromic number is the same whether read from left to right or right to left. For example $41514$ is a palindromic number.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Which of the following is the best estimate for the length of a bus?

- $0.2\ \text{km}$ 
- $2\ \text{m}$ 
- $20\ \text{cm}$ 
- $20 000\ \text{mm}$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Which of the following is the best estimate for the length of a bus?
<emptyline>
- $0.2\ \text{km}$ 
- $2\ \text{m}$ 
- $20\ \text{cm}$ 
- $20 000\ \text{mm}$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>

**Formulas**

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let's convert all options to meters to compare with a typical bus length (approximately $10$ to $15 \ \text{m}$ )

|  **Options** |         **in $\text{m}$**         | **Comment**                                             |
| :-----------------: | :-------------------------------------: | :------------------------------------------------------ |
|   $0.2\ \text{km}$  |    $0.2 \times 1000 = 200\ \text{m}$    | Too long for a bus                                  |
|    $2\ \text{m}$    |              $2\ \text{m}$              | Short (size of a small car)                    |
|   $20\ \text{cm}$   |    $\dfrac{20}{100} = 0.2\ \text{m}$    | Much too short (length of a ruler)                      |
| $20000\ \text{mm}$ | $\dfrac{20000}{1000} = 20\ \text{m}$ | Best estimate  |

Answer $= 20000 \ \text{mm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="option" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Option**

<p>D</p>
</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20000 \ \text{mm}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Work out the number from the following clues:

- It is a whole number.
- It is less than $100$.
- It is a square number.
- It is one less than a multiple of $5$.
- $16$ is a factor of this number.


</div>

- It is one less than a multiple of $5$.
- $16$ is a factor of this number.
<emptyline>
</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

There are $10 \ \text{millimetres}$ in a centimetre and $100 \ \text{centimetres}$ in a metre.

How many millimetres are there in $25.1 \ \text{metres}$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">There are $10 \ \text{millimetres}$ in a centimetre and $100 \ \text{centimetres}$ in a metre.
<emptyline>
How many millimetres are there in $25.1 \ \text{metres}$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 25.1 \ \text{m} \\\\
&= 25.1 \times 100 \ \text{cm} \\\\
&= 25.1 \times 100 \times 10 \ \text{mm} \\\\
&= 25100 \ \text{mm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$25100 \ \text{mm}$

</div>

**Question**

How many numbers can he make that are bigger than $7000?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The possible arrangements are:

- $7135$
- $7153$
- $7315$
- $7351$
- $7513$
- $7531$

Count $= 6$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

For a four-digit number to be bigger than $7000$, the first digit (the thousands digit) must be $7$.

Using permutation for the hundreds, tens and ones places:

Number of digits that can be used in the hundreds place $= 3$

Number of digits that can be used in the tens place $= 2$

Number of digits that can be used in the ones place $= 1$

Count $= 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

Number of digits that can be used in the hundreds place $= 3$
<emptyline>
Number of digits that can be used in the tens place $= 2$
<emptyline>
Number of digits that can be used in the ones place $= 1$
<emptyline>
Count $= 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let's list the square numbers around this range.

| $n$ | Calculation               | $> 101$ and $< 200?$ |
|:---:|:--------------------------:|:------------------------:|
| $10$ | $10 \times 10 = 100$      | No |
| $11$ | $11 \times 11 = 121$      | Yes |
| $12$ | $12 \times 12 = 144$      | Yes |
| $13$ | $13 \times 13 = 169$      | Yes |
| $14$ | $14 \times 14 = 196$      | Yes |
| $15$ | $15 \times 15 = 225$      | No |

Count $= 4$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

**Question**

Which is bigger:

$3^4$ or $4^3?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Which is bigger:
<emptyline>

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{First value}  &= 3 ^ 4 \\\\
                    &= 3 \times 3 \times 3 \times 3 \\\\
                    &= 9 \times 9 \\\\
                    &= 81 \\\\
\text{Second value} &= 4 ^ 3 \\\\
                    &= 4 \times 4 \times 4 \\\\
                    &= 16 \times 4 \\\\
                    &= 64
\end{aligned}
$

$3 ^ 4 > 4 ^ 3$
</div>

**Question**

The area of a postage stamp is calculated as:

$2 \ \text{cm} \times 2.5 \ \text{cm} = 5 \ \text{cm}^2$

What is the area of this stamp in $\text{mm}^2?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<emptyline>

</code></pre>

\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Two square numbers have a difference of $33$. Identify the two missing whole numbers that complete this calculation.

$A^2 - B^2 = 33$

Fill in the two empty boxes to show your answer:

$\boxed{\phantom{1}} \ ^2 - \boxed{\phantom{1}} \ ^2 = 33$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Two square numbers have a difference of $33$. Identify the two missing whole numbers that complete this calculation.
<emptyline>
$A^2 - B^2 = 33$
<emptyline>
Fill in the two empty boxes to show your answer:
<emptyline>
$\boxed{\phantom{1}} \ ^2 - \boxed{\phantom{1}} \ ^2 = 33$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

We can infer the values by using trial and error. Let's start with $6$ and go up, since $5^2 = 25$ which is less than $33$.

Let's test pairs of square numbers to find a difference of $33$.

| $A$ | $B$ | Calculation                          | $=33?$ |
|:---:|:---:|:-------------------------------------:|:-----------------:|
| $6$ | $1$ | $6^2 - 1^2 = 36 - 1 = 35$             | No |
| $6$ | $2$ | $6^2 - 2^2 = 36 - 4 = 32$             | No |
| $7$ | $1$ | $7^2 - 1^2 = 49 - 1 = 48$             | No |
| $7$ | $2$ | $7^2 - 2^2 = 49 - 4 = 45$             | No |
| $7$ | $3$ | $7^2 - 3^2 = 49 - 9 = 40$             | No |
| $7$ | $4$ | $7^2 - 4^2 = 49 - 16 = 33$            | Yes |

The pair that works is $A = 7$ and $B = 4$.

$A = 7$, $B = 4$
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

A fraction will be bigger than $\dfrac{1}{2}$ if twice of its numerator is bigger than the denominator.

Lets calculate for each fraction:

|   **Fraction**   | **$2n$** | **Compare** | **$> \tfrac12$?** |
| :--------------: | :------: | :---------: | :---------------: |
|  $\dfrac{3}{5}$  |    $6$   |   $6 > 5$   |      Yes     |
|  $\dfrac{3}{7}$  |    $6$   |   $6 > 7$   |         No        |
|  $\dfrac{5}{12}$ |   $10$   |  $10 > 12$  |         No        |
|  $\dfrac{8}{15}$ |   $16$   |  $16 > 15$  |     Yes      |
| $\dfrac{11}{20}$ |   $22$   |  $22 > 20$  |     Yes      |

Answer $= \dfrac{3}{5}, \dfrac{8}{15}, \dfrac{11}{20} $
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$a * b$ means multiply the two numbers together and then subtract the larger.

So:

$
\begin{aligned}
4 * 6 &= 24 - 6 \\\\
          &= 18
\end{aligned}
$

Find the value of $8 * 3$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$a * b$ means multiply the two numbers together and then subtract the larger.
<emptyline>
So:
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
4 * 6 &= 24 - 6 \\\\
          &= 18
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Find the value of $8 * 3$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 8 * 3 \\\\
&= (8 \times 3) - 8 \\\\
&= 24 - 8 \\\\
&= 16
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$16$

</div>

**Question**

What is $4 \times (6.2 + 1.05)$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 4 \times (6.2 + 1.05)  \\\\
&= 4 \times 7.25 \\\\
&= 29
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

To convert kilometers to miles I multiply by $5$ and then divide by $8$.

Using this method how many miles is $240 \ \text{kilometers}$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">To convert kilometers to miles I multiply by $5$ and then divide by $8$.
<emptyline>
Using this method how many miles is $240 \ \text{kilometers}$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&=  240 \ \text {kilometers} \\\\
&=  (240 \times 5) \div 8 \ \text {miles} \\\\
&=  \dfrac {240 \times 5} {8} \\\\
&=  \dfrac {8 \times 30 \times 5} {8} \\\\
&=  \dfrac {\cancel {8} \times 30 \times 5} {\cancel {8}} \\\\
&=  30 \times 5 \\\\
&=  150 \ \text {miles}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$150 \ \text {miles}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

What is the square root of $225?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Which of these lengths is longest?

$42\ \text{cm} \quad  0.4 \ \text{m} \quad  147 \ \text{mm} \quad  0.351 \ \text{m} \quad  33 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Which of these lengths is longest?
<emptyline>
$42\ \text{cm} \quad  0.4 \ \text{m} \quad  147 \ \text{mm} \quad  0.351 \ \text{m} \quad  33 \ \text{cm}$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let's convert all the units to cm. 

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 42 \ \text{cm}, \quad 0.4 \ \text{m}, \quad 147 \ \text{mm}, \quad 0.351 \ \text{m}, \quad 33  \ \text{cm} \\\\
&= 42 \ \text{cm}, \quad 0.4 \times 100 \ \text{cm}, \quad \dfrac {147} {10} \ \text{cm}, \quad 0.351 \times 100 \ \text{cm}, \quad 33  \ \text{cm} \\\\
&= 42 \ \text{cm}, \quad 40 \ \text{cm}, \quad 14.7 \ \text{cm}, \quad 35.1 \ \text{cm}, \quad 33  \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Longest length $= 42 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$42 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

\end{aligned}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is $36 \div (9 + 3)?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is $36 \div (9 + 3)?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: Using BIDMAS
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 36 \div (9 + 3) \\\\
&= \dfrac {36} {12} \\\\
&= \dfrac {12 \times 3} {12} \\\\
&= \dfrac {\cancel {12} \times 3} {\cancel {12}} \\\\
&= 3
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$3$

</div>

**Question**

If $432.6 \times 7 = 3028.2$

What is $43.26 \times 0.7 ?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

&= \dfrac {3028.2}{100} \\\\

\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Calculate how much bigger is $3\dfrac{1}{4}$ is than $1\dfrac{3}{4}$ writing your answer as a decimal.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Calculate how much bigger is $3\dfrac{1}{4}$ is than $1\dfrac{3}{4}$ writing your answer as a decimal.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 3 \dfrac {1} {4} - 1 \dfrac {3} {4} \\\\
&= \dfrac {13} {4} - \dfrac {7} {4} \\\\
&= \dfrac {13 - 7} {4} \\\\
&= \dfrac {6} {4} \\\\
&= \dfrac {3 \times 2} {2 \times 2} \\\\
&= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {2}} {2 \times \cancel {2}} \\\\
&= \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\
&= 1.5
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$1.5$

</div>

This process continues until all riders have been given a unique number that identifies them individually, but also identifies which team they are on.

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Subtract $7 + (3 \times 11)$ from $(7 + 3) \times 11$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Subtract $7 + (3 \times 11)$ from $(7 + 3) \times 11$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: Using BIDMAS
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= \big( (7 + 3) \times 11 \big) - \big( (7 + (3 \times 11)) \big) \\\\
&= (10 \times 11) - (7 + 33) \\\\
&= 110 - 40 \\\\
&= 70
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$70$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Circle which of the following has a different value from the others:

- $3 - 7 - 4$
- $(3 - 7) - 4$
- $3 - (7 - 4)$
- $((3 - 7) - 4)$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Circle which of the following has a different value from the others:
<emptyline>
- $3 - 7 - 4$
- $(3 - 7) - 4$
- $3 - (7 - 4)$
- $((3 - 7) - 4)$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{A} &= 3 - 7 - 4 \\\\
         &= -8 \\\\
\text{B} &= (3 - 7) - 4 \\\\
         &= -4 - 4 \\\\
         &= -8 \\\\
\text{C} &= 3 - (7 - 4) \\\\
         &= 3 - 3 \\\\ 
         &= 0 \\\\
\text{D} &= ((3 - 7) - 4) \\\\ 
         &= (-4 - 4) \\\\
         &= -8
\end{aligned}
$

Different Value $= 3 - (7 - 4)$
</div>
</div>

</div>

**Answer**

$3 - (7 - 4)$

</div>
</div>

Calculate $0.35 + \dfrac{3}{5} - \dfrac{1}{4}$, leaving your answer as a decimal.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

\begin{aligned}

&= 0.35 + 0.6 - 0.25 \\\\
&= 0.95 - 0.25 \\\\
&= 0.7
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Subtract $4 + (2 \times 13)$ from $(4 + 2) \times 13$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Subtract $4 + (2 \times 13)$ from $(4 + 2) \times 13$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: Using BIDMAS
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

\begin{aligned}
&= \big( (4 + 2) \times 13 \big) - \big( 4 + (2 \times 13) \big) \\\\
&= (6 \times 13) - (4 + 26) \\\\
&= 78 - 30 \\\\
&= 48
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Calculate $0.75 + \dfrac{2}{5} + \dfrac{17}{100}$, leaving your answer as a decimal.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Calculate $0.75 + \dfrac{2}{5} + \dfrac{17}{100}$, leaving your answer as a decimal.
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>

\begin{aligned}

&= 0.75 + 0.4 + 0.17\\\\
&= 1.32
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Write down a fraction whose numerator and denominator are both whole
numbers and whose value is between $\dfrac{7}{13}$ and $\dfrac{8}{13}$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Subtract $20 + (1 \times 7)$ from $(20 + 1) \times 7$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Subtract $20 + (1 \times 7)$ from $(20 + 1) \times 7$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: Using BIDMAS
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= \big( (20 + 1) \times 7 \big) - \big( 20 + (1 \times 7) \big) \\\\
&= (21 \times 7) - (20 + 7) \\\\
&= 147 - 27 \\\\
&= 120
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Calculate $0.35 + \dfrac{4}{5} + \dfrac{37}{100}$, leaving your answer as a decimal. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Calculate $0.35 + \dfrac{4}{5} + \dfrac{37}{100}$, leaving your answer as a decimal. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 0.35 + \dfrac {4} {5} + \dfrac {37} {100} \\\\
&= 0.35 + \dfrac {4 \times 2} {5 \times 2} + \dfrac {37} {100} \\\\
&= 0.35+ \dfrac {8} {10} + \dfrac {37} {100} \\\\
&= 0.35 + 0.8 + 0.37 \\\\
&= 1.52
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
21 - (a \times 3) &= 9 \\\\
21 - 3a           &= 9 \\\\
3a                &= 21-9 \\\\
3a                &= 12 \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {12} {3} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac{4 \times 3}{3} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac{4 \times \cancel 3}{\cancel 3} \\\\
a                 &= 4
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

&= 0.4 + 0.25 + 0.27 \\\\
&= 0.92
\end{aligned}
$

Write $\dfrac{51}{60}$ as a decimal.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Write $\dfrac{51}{60}$ as a decimal.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= \dfrac {51} {60} \\\\
&= \dfrac {17 \times 3} {20 \times 3} \\\\
&= \dfrac {17 \times \cancel {3}} {20 \times \cancel {3}} \\\\
&= \dfrac {17} {20} \\\\
&= \dfrac {17 \times 5} {20 \times 5} \\\\
&= \dfrac {85} {100} \\\\
&= 0.85
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Three bus services stop at my bus stop. Service $A$ departs every $3 \ \text{minutes}$, service $B$ every $5 \ \text{minutes}$ 
and service $C$ every $8 \ \text{minutes}$.

If all three services leave my stop at $10.00 \ \text{a.m.}$, at what time will they next leave my stop together? (Assume that all three services always run on time). 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Three bus services stop at my bus stop. Service $A$ departs every $3 \ \text{minutes}$, service $B$ every $5 \ \text{minutes}$ 
and service $C$ every $8 \ \text{minutes}$.
<emptyline>
If all three services leave my stop at $10.00 \ \text{a.m.}$, at what time will they next leave my stop together? (Assume that all three services always run on time). 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

LCM of $3, 5$ and $8 = 120$

After $120 \ \text{minutes}$, three bus services will leave the stop together.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Time at which three services will next leave stop together}   &= 10{:}00 \ \text{a.m.} + 120 \ \text{minutes} \\\\
                                                                    &= 2{:}00 \ \text{a.m.}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the answer when the first prime number is subtracted from the first even multiple of $7?$

-  $5$
-  $11$
-  $12$
-  $13$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

-  $12$
-  $13$ 
</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Here are $2$ number machines:

![papers/eltham-college/2019/sample-paper-1/s01-q20-i00.png](/assets/papers/eltham-college/2019/sample-paper-1/s01-q20-i00.png "papers/eltham-college/2019/sample-paper-1/s01-q20-i00.png")

Both machines have the same input.
Work out the input if both machines also have the same output.

- $2$
- $-2$
- $6$
- $-6$

</div>

</code></pre>

n                                                &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

(n \times 4) + 4                                 &= (n \times 5) - 2 \\\\
4n + 4                                           &= 5n -2 \\\\
4 + 2                                            &= 5n - 4n \\\\
n                                                &= 6
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is $(999 - 99 + 9) \div 9?$

- $99$
- $100$
- $101$
- $109$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is $(999 - 99 + 9) \div 9?$
<emptyline>
- $99$
- $100$
- $101$
- $109$ 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: Using BIDMAS
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= (999 - 99 + 9) \div 9 \\\\
&= (900 + 9) \div 9 \\\\
&= \dfrac {909} {9} \\\\
&= \dfrac {9 \times 101} {9} \\\\
&= \dfrac {\cancel{9} \times 101} {\cancel{9}} \\\\
&= 101
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

as when it is divided by $3?$

- $5$
- $7$
- $9$
- $11$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the value of $19 + 99 + 19 \times 99?$

- $1999$
- $11701$
- $13563$
- None of these 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the value of $19 + 99 + 19 \times 99?$
<emptyline>
- $1999$
- $11701$
- $13563$
- None of these 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

\begin{aligned}
&= 19 + 99 + 19 \times 99 \\\\
&= 99 + 19 + 19 \times 99 \\\\
&= 99 + 19 \times 1 + 19 \times 99 \\\\
&= 99 + 19 \times (1 +  99) \\\\
&= 99 + 19 \times 100 \\\\
&= 99 + 1900 \\\\
&= 1999
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

Which one of these calculations is **incorrect**?

- $4 \times 5 + 67 = 45 + 6 \times 7$
- $3 \times 7 + 48 = 37 + 4 \times 8$
- $2 \times 5 + 69 = 25 + 6 \times 9$
- $9 \times 6 + 73 = 96 + 7 \times 3$ 

</div>

</code></pre>

- $2010$

Use your answers to part A) to find $47 \%$ of $90$.

Show your working out.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</code></pre>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 47 \% \ \text {of} \ 90 \\\\
&= (40 \% + 5 \% + 2 \%) \ \text {of} \ 90 \\\\
&= 40 \% \ \text {of} \ 90 + 5 \% \ \text {of} \ 90 + 2 \% \ \text {of} \ 90 \\\\
&= 4 \times 10 \% \ \text {of} \ 90 + 4.5 + 2 \times 1 \% \ \text {of} \ 90 \\\\
&= 4 \times 9 + 4.5 + 2 \times 0.9 \\\\
&= 36 + 4.5 + 1.8 \\\\
&= 42.3
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

What was the total and how could this be done?

**Question**

What number is halfway between $-3$ and $8?$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

&= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 5\\\\

&= 2.5
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$36$ is a square number because it can be written $6 \times 6$.

Similarly, $64 = 8 \times 8$ is a square number.

$1000$ is a cube number because it can be written $10 \times 10 \times 10$

Similarly, $343 = 7 \times 7 \times 7$ is a cube number.

The French mathematician Pierre de Fermat claimed correctly that there is only one square number that is $2$ less than a cube number.

It is less than $50$.

What is it? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$36$ is a square number because it can be written $6 \times 6$.
<emptyline>
Similarly, $64 = 8 \times 8$ is a square number.
<emptyline>
$1000$ is a cube number because it can be written $10 \times 10 \times 10$
<emptyline>
Similarly, $343 = 7 \times 7 \times 7$ is a cube number.
<emptyline>
The French mathematician Pierre de Fermat claimed correctly that there is only one square number that is $2$ less than a cube number.
<emptyline>
It is less than $50$.
<emptyline>
What is it? 
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

<div class="formula">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is halfway between $120$ and $300?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>

</code></pre>

\begin{aligned}
&= \dfrac {1} {2} \times (120 + 300) \\\\
&= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 420\\\\
&= \dfrac {2 \times 210} {2} \\\\
&= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 210} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
&= 210
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many centimetres are there in $1.4 \ \text{metres}?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many centimetres are there in $1.4 \ \text{metres}?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 1.4 \ \text {metres} \\\\
&= 1.4 \times 100 \ \text {cm} \\\\
&= 140 \ \text {cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$140 \ \text {cm}$

**Question**

Jaishan uses this to find $83 \times 83 - 17 \times 17$ **WITHOUT** using long multiplication.

How did he do it and what is the answer?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

&= 83 ^ {2} - 17 ^ {2} \\\\

&= 6600
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

My calculator is broken. The only buttons that work are these.

$
\large {
\boxed{4}      \quad
\boxed{7}      \quad
\boxed{\times} \quad
\boxed{-}      \quad
\boxed{=}
}
$


Which sequence of buttons will enable me to get an answer of $11$ on the screen of my calculator?

If you have time, try to find some more ways to get $11$.

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Here are three numbers
and two operations on five cards.

$\huge{ \boxed{\phantom{}3} \ \boxed{\phantom{}7} \ \boxed{24} \ \boxed{\phantom{}+} \ \boxed{\phantom{}\div} } $

Which of these gives the answer $15?$

- $24 \div 7 + 3$
- $3 + 7 \div 24$
- $7 + 3 \div 24$
- $3 \div 7 + 24$
- $24 \div 3 + 7$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Here are three numbers
and two operations on five cards.
<emptyline>
$\huge{ \boxed{\phantom{}3} \ \boxed{\phantom{}7} \ \boxed{24} \ \boxed{\phantom{}+} \ \boxed{\phantom{}\div} } $
<emptyline>
Which of these gives the answer $15?$
<emptyline>
- $24 \div 7 + 3$
- $3 + 7 \div 24$
- $7 + 3 \div 24$
- $3 \div 7 + 24$
- $24 \div 3 + 7$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: Using BIDMAS
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{A}    &= 24 \div 7 + 3 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {24} {7} + 3 \\\\
            &= 3 \dfrac{3}{7} + 3 \\\\
            &= 6 \dfrac{3}{7} \neq \red{15} \\\\
\text{B}    &= 3 + 7 \div 24 \\\\
            &= 3 + \dfrac {7} {24} \\\\
            &= 3 \dfrac{7}{24} \neq \red{15} \\\\
\text{C}    &= 7 + 3 \div 24 \\\\
            &= 7 + \dfrac {3} {24} \\\\
            &= 7 + \dfrac {3} {3 \times 8} \\\\
            &= 7 + \dfrac {\cancel {3}} {\cancel {3} \times 8} \\\\
            &= 7 + \dfrac {1} {8} \\\\
            &= 7 \dfrac{1}{8} \neq \red{15} \\\\
\text{D}    &= 3 \div 7 + 24 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {3} {7} + 24 \\\\
            &= 24 \dfrac {3}{7} \neq \red{15} \\\\
\text{E}    &= 24 \div 3 + 7 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {24} {3} + 7 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {3 \times 8} {3} + 7 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 8} {\cancel {3}} + 7 \\\\
            &= 8 + 7 \\\\
            &= \green{15}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="option" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Option**

<p>E</p>
</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$24 \div 3 + 7$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="tipcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Tips Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">- rtq_abbr_note_md_bidmas
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="formulacodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="formulacodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Formulas Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%
</code></pre>

<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
\text{A}    &= 24 \div 7 + 3 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {24} {7} + 3 \\\\
            &= 3 \dfrac{3}{7} + 3 \\\\
            &= 6 \dfrac{3}{7} \neq \rtq_abbr_working_color_wrong_answer{15} \\\\
\text{B}    &= 3 + 7 \div 24 \\\\
            &= 3 + \dfrac {7} {24} \\\\
            &= 3 \dfrac{7}{24} \neq \rtq_abbr_working_color_wrong_answer{15} \\\\
\text{C}    &= 7 + 3 \div 24 \\\\
            &= 7 + \dfrac {3} {24} \\\\
            &= 7 + \dfrac {3} {3 \times 8} \\\\
            &= 7 + \dfrac {\cancel {3}} {\cancel {3} \times 8} \\\\
            &= 7 + \dfrac {1} {8} \\\\
            &= 7 \dfrac{1}{8} \neq \rtq_abbr_working_color_wrong_answer{15} \\\\
\text{D}    &= 3 \div 7 + 24 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {3} {7} + 24 \\\\
            &= 24 \dfrac {3}{7} \neq \rtq_abbr_working_color_wrong_answer{15} \\\\
\text{E}    &= 24 \div 3 + 7 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {24} {3} + 7 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {3 \times 8} {3} + 7 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 8} {\cancel {3}} + 7 \\\\
            &= 8 + 7 \\\\
            &= \rtq_abbr_working_color_answer{15}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>

**Question**

In a 'third off' sale a bike is sold for $\pounds 114$.
How much would it have sold for before the sale?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

</code></pre>

<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the original price (in $\pounds$) $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {1} {3} \ \text{of} \ a      &= 114 \\\\
\dfrac {1} {3} \times a             &= 114 \\\\
a                                   &= 114 \times 3 \\\\
a                                   &= \pounds 342
\end{aligned}
$

Original price $= \pounds 342$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many thousands are there in one million?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many thousands are there in one million?
</code></pre>

                            &= \dfrac {1000 \times 1000} {1000} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {1000 \times \cancel{1000}} {\cancel{1000}} \\\\
                            &= 1000
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Write down a number between $0.3$ and $\dfrac{2}{5}$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Write down a number between $0.3$ and $\dfrac{2}{5}$.
</code></pre>

<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= \dfrac {1} {2} \times (0.3 + \dfrac {2} {5}) \\\\
&= \dfrac {1} {2} \times (0.3 + 0.4) \\\\
&= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 0.7 \\\\
&= \dfrac {0.7} {2} \\\\
&= 0.35
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

&= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 0.7 \\\\
&= \dfrac {0.7} {2} \\\\
&= 0.35
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Which of these could be the correct measurement for the length of a bus? 

- $140\ \text{m}$ 
- $1400\ \text{cm}$ 
- $140\ \text{mm}$ 
- $140 000\ \text{mm}$ 
- $0.0014\ \text{km}$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Which of these could be the correct measurement for the length of a bus? 
<emptyline>
- $140\ \text{m}$ 
- $1400\ \text{cm}$ 
- $140\ \text{mm}$ 
- $140 000\ \text{mm}$ 
- $0.0014\ \text{km}$ 
</code></pre>
</div>

**Working**

Let's convert all options to meters to compare with a typical bus length (approximately $10$ to $15\ \text{m}$).

|  **Options** |         **in $\text{m}$**         | **Comment**                                             |
| :-----------------: | :-------------------------------------: | :------------------------------------------------------ |
| $140\ \text{m}$       | $140\ \text{m}$                             | Too long                      |
| $1400\ \text{cm}$     | $\dfrac{1400}{100} = 14\ \text{m}$          | Reasonable bus length                      |
| $140\ \text{mm}$      | $\dfrac{140}{1000} = 0.14\ \text{m}$        | Much too short                             |
| $140000\ \text{mm}$   | $\dfrac{140000}{1000} = 140\ \text{m}$      | Far too long                               |
| $0.0014\ \text{km}$   | $0.0014 \times 1000 = 1.4\ \text{m}$        | Much too short                             |

Answer $= 1400\ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>

**Question**

Amran wrote down the calculation:

$\dfrac{6000 \times 20} {30} = 40$

Her teacher looked at the answer and said it could not be correct.

Explain how her teacher knew the answer must be wrong.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

**Working**

$\dfrac{6000 \times 20} {30} = 40$

Lets verify.

$
\begin{aligned}
&= \dfrac{6000 \times 20} {30} \\\\ 
&= \dfrac{30 \times 200 \times 20} {30} \\\\
&= \dfrac{\cancel{30} \times 200 \times 20} {\cancel{30}} \\\\
&= 200 \times 20 \\\\
&= 4000
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

a                       &= 12
\end{aligned}

**Question**

Using all $5$ cards what is the number that is closest to $50000?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

To be close to $50000$, the number should start with $4$ (approaching from below) or $6$ (approaching from above).

For the number closest to $50000$ starting with $4$, we want the largest possible value, so $48762$

Difference: $50000 - 48762 = 1238$

For the number closest to $50000$ starting with $6$, we want the smallest possible value, so $62478$

Difference: $62478 - 50000 = 12478$

$1238$ is smaller than $12478$, so $48762$ is the closest.

Number $= 48762$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">To be close to $50000$, the number should start with $4$ (approaching from below) or $6$ (approaching from above).
<emptyline>
For the number closest to $50000$ starting with $4$, we want the largest possible value, so $48762$
<emptyline>
Difference: $50000 - 48762 = 1238$
<emptyline>
For the number closest to $50000$ starting with $6$, we want the smallest possible value, so $62478$
<emptyline>
Difference: $62478 - 50000 = 12478$
<emptyline>
$1238$ is smaller than $12478$, so $48762$ is the closest.
<emptyline>
Number $= 48762$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$2 \dfrac{3}{5} + 1 \dfrac{1}{2}$
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

\begin{aligned}
&= 2 \dfrac {3} {5} + 1 \dfrac {1} {2} \\\\
&= \dfrac {13} {5} + \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\

&= \dfrac {26} {10} + \dfrac {15} {10} \\\\
&= \dfrac {26 + 15} {10} \\\\
&= \dfrac {41} {10} \\\\
&= 4 \dfrac {1} {10} 
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Arrange the digits $7, 6, 5,$ and $4$ so that the resulting number is closest to five thousand.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Arrange the digits $7, 6, 5,$ and $4$ so that the resulting number is closest to five thousand.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

To be close to $5000$, the number should start with $4$ (approaching from below) or $5$ (approaching from above).

For the number closest to $5000$ starting with $4$, we want the largest possible value, so $4765$. The difference is $5000 - 4765 = 235$.

For the number closest to $5000$ starting with $5$, we want the smallest possible value, so $5467$. The difference is $5467 - 5000 = 467$.

$235$ is smaller than $467$, so $4765$ is the nearest.

Answer $= 4765$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4765$

</div>
</div>

<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">To be close to $5000$, the number should start with $4$ (approaching from below) or $5$ (approaching from above).
<emptyline>
For the number closest to $5000$ starting with $4$, we want the largest possible value, so $4765$. The difference is $5000 - 4765 = 235$.
<emptyline>
For the number closest to $5000$ starting with $5$, we want the smallest possible value, so $5467$. The difference is $5467 - 5000 = 467$.
<emptyline>
$235$ is smaller than $467$, so $4765$ is the nearest.
<emptyline>
Answer $= 4765$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Write down two different odd prime numbers that add together to make a square number.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Write down two different odd prime numbers that add together to make a square number.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

ABBR: Square numbers between $1$ and $50= 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49$


We need $2$ different odd prime numbers that add together to make a square number.

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error.

| Square | Prime pair          | Works? |
|:------:|:-------------------:|:------:|
| $16$   | $3 + 13 = 16$       | Yes |
| $16$   | $5 + 11 = 16$       | Yes |
| $36$   | $5 + 31 = 36$       | Yes |
| $36$   | $7 + 29 = 36$       | Yes |
| $36$   | $13 + 23 = 36$      | Yes |
| $36$   | $17 + 19 = 36$      | Yes |


Answer $= (3, 13), (5, 11)$

</div>
</div>
